rows.claim: Turing needs a diffusion ratio >= 10
rows.witness: messages/2026-10-31-DIFFUSION-GAP-KILLED.md: Lean-checked J=[[1,-1],[1011/1000,-101/100]], Du=1, Dv=1.1, L=5pi Neumann, mode-1 det=-21/25000 (codex-api); closed form r*=(sqrt(det J)+sqrt(-bc))^2/a^2 is classical (Murray)
rows.allowed: There is no universal diffusion-ratio threshold; the required ratio depends on the kinetics (two-species floor r*>1).

rows.claim: Real proteins cannot reach the required diffusion ratio
rows.witness: messages/2026-10-31-DELPHI-FRAMING-AND-DIFFUSION-VERDICT.md; critic note planning/rethink/critic-diffusion-ratio.md (Mueller 2012 Science 336:721 measured Nodal/Lefty effective ratio; Kuhn 2022 Nat Commun: binding/retention, not size)
rows.allowed: Effective ratios in tissue are set by binding and retention (Mueller 2012; Kuhn 2022); a bare Stokes-Einstein ratio is not the relevant quantity.

rows.claim: Physics knows where its equations stop; biology does not (as a novelty claim)

rows.allowed: The finite-domain scope caveats are textbook; what we built is a checkable, versioned statement of them.

rows.claim: `finite_domain_stable` Lean theorem advertised as finite-domain STABILITY (its premise was determinant non-negativity)
rows.kind: mis-operationalised (determinant nonnegativity advertised as stability; NOT vacuous premises)
rows.witness: Codex commit b4e60db: planning/rethink/CODEX-21-CLAIM-FREEZE-REVIEW.md (original theorem paragraph) and the exact source snapshot artifacts/integration/codex-api/admissible-review/Admissible.lean (sha256 c51b98a8c4218c5e272223c5d710de0d765804d78beace544850f9749cf07236); messages/codex-price-probe-progress.md states the finding. Analytic witness J=diag(2,2), Du=Dv=1, L=pi: D(q)=(2-q)^2>=0 for all q satisfies the premise, yet mode n=1 (q=1) has both growth eigenvalues +1 (no new Lean compile of this witness is claimed). A stronger theorem `finite_domain_linearly_stable` was added later (commit 469874b; compiled by Codex at 7f9035a), so the historical defect was partly repaired. Earlier ledger text describing it as 'not_lt / saying nothing' came from THE-REFRAME and is NOT the accurate description.
rows.allowed: A theorem whose premise is determinant non-negativity was advertised as stability; the premise holds for unstable systems. It compiled and passed an axiom audit, which shows those checks do not establish that a statement means what its name says.

rows.claim: Thompson d~h^(3/2) refuted by a pooled Tallo regression

rows.allowed: A pooled OLS tests mean allometry, not Thompson's buckling limit; no slope here confirms or refutes the claim.

summary.method: kill_recorded - claim_stated in minutes, only where both times are derivable and ordered; times are file mtimes (messages) or git commit times; mtime = last modification, commit time = commit not utterance, so durations are rough, may be inflated or deflated, and rows differ in kind (prior-art lookups, audits, measurements)
summary.reading: descriptive of THIS team on THIS day; not a rate, not generalisable; do not put the median on a slide without n and method and without the not-derivable rows
summary.caught_by_class_note: explicit per-row classification (v2): substring matching on caught_by text was wrong (R18 'not independently confirmed' matched 'independent'). author = caught only by the author's own measurement or rule (all three are measurements/rules, not reviews); mixed = author found it and an independent hold/review also applied

notes: Message files have only mtimes; THE-REFRAME's own text labels itself '09:05 PDT' but its mtime is 07:27; use mtimes/commit times, not labels inside files.

claim_stated for R06 is not derivable (no dated statement located); its kill time is the recorded-review commit time of b4e60db (Codex), not a first-utterance time. R17: the acceptance rule was written in the script before the first run and the result was committed together with it, so a claim-to-kill duration is not meaningful (left not derivable). R01/R02 use the earliest kill-recording file (primary-prior-art-verdict.md); later files (POST-AUDIT, ATLAS) add further witnesses.
